messages.content: Who are the famous dancers of the 19th Century?

function.name: get_museum_artists
function.description: Retrieves a list of all artists whose works are present in a museum during a particular period. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

period.description: The time period for which to retrieve the artists, e.g., 19th Century.

country.description: The country where the museum is located, optional parameter. Default: 'USA'

message.content:
**Famous Dancers of the 19th Century**

| Name | Nationality | Notable Contributions |
|------|-------------|-----------------------|
| **Marie Taglioni** (1804–1884) | Swedish | Pioneered the romantic ballet style; known for her ethereal presence and the “floating” technique. She danced the title role in *La Sylphide* (1832). |
| **Carlo Blasis** (1815–1890) | Italian | A virtuoso dancer and teacher who helped shape modern ballet technique. |
| **Carl Maria von Weber** (1786–1826) | German | Though primarily a composer, his music inspired many ballets of the era. |
| **Fanny Elssler** (1810–1879) | Austrian | Renowned for her dramatic expressiveness and technical brilliance; performed across Europe and America. |
| **Enrico Cecchetti** (1850–1928) | Italian | Developed the Cecchetti method, a foundational ballet training system still used today. |
| **Marius Petipa** (1818–1910) | Russian | While best known as a choreographer, he was also a skilled dancer and created many iconic roles. |
| **Jules Perrot** (1793–1869) | French | A celebrated dancer and choreographer; introduced the “Pas de deux” concept. |
| **Caroline Hübbe** (1841–1907) | German | Known for her lyrical style and contributions to the development of the Romantic ballet. |
| **Anna Pavlova** (1881–1931) | Russian | Although she rose to prominence slightly later, her early career began in the late 19th century; she popularized the “doll” style of ballet. |
| **George Balanchine** (1904–1983) | Russian-American | Started dancing in the 1920s but was influenced heavily by 19th-century ballet traditions. |

These dancers were instrumental in shaping the evolution of ballet during the 19th century, each bringing unique styles and techniques that influenced generations of performers that followed.
